request.spec:
When a person is edited, the form remembers which version of the person it loaded. If someone
else has saved that person in the meantime, saving is refused with an error on the form, nothing
is stored, and the form shows the current values; opening the editor again and saving works.
Submitting any form twice before the first submit has answered stores one record, not two.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a person is edited, the form remembers which version of the person it loaded. If someone
else has saved that person in the meantime, saving is refused with an error on the form, nothing
is stored, and the form shows the current values; opening the editor again and saving works.
Submitting any form twice before the first submit has answered stores one record, not two.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I made the change and `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 acceptance tests are green.

**Edit conflict (stale edits are refused)**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V12__person_version.sql`, adds a `version` column to `person`. `Person` now has a JPA `@Version` field, so the version goes up by one on every save.
- **Server:** the version is now included in what the screen gets for each person, and saving an edit (`PUT /people/{id}`) must send back the version the editor loaded. If the stored version is different, the save is refused with HTTP 412. If two saves land at the same moment, the second one fails the database's version check and gets the same 412. Either way nothing is stored, and because the audit record is only written when a save goes through, no `PERSON_EDITED` line is written.
- **Front end:** the person form remembers the version it loaded. On a 412 it re-reads the people from the store, shows a message in `person-form-error`, and keeps the editor open with the current values.

One choice you may want to check: after a refusal, the form also picks up the current version. So pressing Save again straight away, on the values now showing, will work without reopening the editor. Reopening and saving also works, as the request asks.

**Double submit stores one record**
The Save buttons were already disabled while a save was running, but the screen only redraws after the click is handled, so a double-click sent the second click before the button turned off. Each form's submit handler now ignores a second submit while the first is still running. That covers the person, claim, rate, sheet-today and sheet-load forms. The guard is only in the browser; the server doesn't detect duplicate requests.
